mechanism: From sales-price vs return theory, derive two break-even prices P1/P2; market price Pm is their arithmetic mean (leopard) and optimal price Popt their geometric mean (lion). Map current price to P2 (bull) or P1 (bear) vs lion/leopard managers: bulls manage → buy regime, bears manage → sell regime, lions manage → flat/beyond-market regime.
data_needed: Recent Ps,St pairs (or Forex OHLC proxy) to estimate elasticity Y and virtual sales S by OLS; Po,v,Cf cost inputs; then P1,P2,Popt,Pm hierarchy.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Goods-market worked example; Forex charts for 2010–2011 and EURUSD/GBPUSD snapshots dated 11.06.2015 00:00 Moscow.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an explicit multi-level virtual-price regime sensor (bull/bear/lion/leopard) grounded in break-even geometry rather than classical MA or oscillator bands.
quote: bulls manage the market — buy; bears manage the market — sell; lions manages the market — beyond market.

mechanism: Trend change is sensed when managing lion/leopard levels intervene: either sharp transfer of price management to the opposite side at any level, or voluntary bull↔bear handoff exactly on the lion (Popt) level; gathering of all levels at lion signals severe flat.
data_needed: Time series of P, Popt (lion), Pm (leopard), P1/P2 relative positions and crossings.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex pairs illustrated (EURUSD, GBPUSD); theory claimed common to goods and Forex.
why_new_for_mis: Frames regime-change as transfer of control among named virtual levels, including a flat-at-lion signature, not just a single indicator cross.
quote: Normally, there are two ways the trend changes: a) at any moment and any price level by a sharp intervention of the managing levels of lion and leopard ... b) voluntary transfer of the price management from bulls to bears on the lion level.

quote: Be careful performing an analysis! Wish you to make a right choice!

mechanism: A level-N TD high (low) is a bar whose high (low) exceeds (is below) highs (lows) of N bars before and N bars after; level 2 equals Bill Williams fractals. Builds a multi-scale extremum sensor parameterized by N.
data_needed: OHLC series; Level input; buffers UpDot/DownDot skipping the forming bar.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any chart symbol/TF in MQL4; demos with Level=1 and Level=10.
why_new_for_mis: Provides a clean, scaleable local-extremum primitive (generalized fractals) usable as structure input for MIS swing/regime pipelines.
quote: If it's required to build a level 2 TD point, then the maximum price of a defined candlestick must be compared with two previous and two following candles.

mechanism: Fit TD lines through the two most recent same-side TD points (y=kx+b); a break of an upward-sloping bearish TD line downward (or downward-sloping bullish TD line upward) plus AddPips confirmation is treated as a trend-change entry.
data_needed: Last two TD highs and two TD lows from iTDDots; line values DU/DD vs prior bar; AddPips.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex charts in MT4 tester examples; Level parameter for TD point depth.
why_new_for_mis: Turns objectively constructed TD trendlines into a break-based regime-change sensor instead of subjective hand-drawn lines.
quote: if a price crosses a TD line and proceeds moving in the same direction, then the trend may change.

mechanism: Map ADX main-line into fuzzy terms low/moderate/medium/high (trapezoid/triangle MFs) and |RVI| into low/medium/high/higher; Mamdani rules fuse them into continuous take-profit add-on categories—soft graded trend-strength sensing rather than hard ADX>30.
data_needed: iADX(period=10) main/+DI/-DI, iRVI(period=10) main/signal on chosen bar; FuzzyNet Mamdani system with configurable MF vertices.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 example; MT4 indicator panel; ADX threshold 30, RVI ±0.1 for signal gate.
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS a continuous fuzzy trend-strength feature that preserves border-zone ambiguity classical hard thresholds discard.
quote: in the boarder values there may be a belonging to not just one specific category as before, but to both simultaneously to a different extent.

mechanism: Custom OnTester criterion: R² of strategy balance or sampled equity vs linear regression (Pearson/Spearman), signed by end-vs-start equity; evaluates EA equity smoothness, not market state.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: CImpulse EA on EURUSD H1/M15, 2015.01–2017.10 optimization.
why_new_for_mis: No market sensing after full read—strategy backtest quality metric only.
quote: R-squared is one of the few metrics that calculate the smoothness of both the balance curve and the floating profit curve of the strategy.

mechanism: Group the 28 majors into 8 baskets by shared base/quote currency; form a unified basket-currency price as the unweighted geometric mean of basket-pair closes (invert pairs where the basket currency is the quote), yielding a USD-index-like sensor of that currency’s strength.
data_needed: Close prices of the seven pairs in the chosen basket; direction flags for inversion; optional comparison to USDX.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AUD/CAD/CHF/EUR/GBP/JPY/NZD/USD baskets; H1 and D1 demos vs USDX; pairs listed in Table 1.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a per-currency strength regime series aggregated across a full major basket, not a single pair oscillator.
quote: we consider the geometric mean calculation equation acceptable for calculating different basket currency status parameters.

mechanism: Apply a parent oscillator (e.g. Stochastic) to each basket pair and average (arithmetic or geometric mean) the readings into a unified overbought/oversold sensor for the basket currency; usable even when geometric mean of prices is inappropriate for signed indicators.
data_needed: Per-pair iStochastic (or RSI/WPR) buffers for all basket members; mean across members each bar.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EUR basket on EURGBP D1 example; Stochastic(5,3,3); same 8-currency basket taxonomy.
why_new_for_mis: Extends classical oscillators into a currency-level OB/OS regime feature that filters pair-local noise.
quote: GBP overbought/oversold status is a common currency status parameter acting as a "unified RSI" showing the status of the basket currency instead of a currency pair.

mechanism: Build combined WPR for base and quote baskets (remap parent WPR from [0,-100] to [-100,100]); distance=(WPR_base−WPR_quote)/2. Signal when distance approaches ±100, reverses, and closes beyond ±60 (OB/OS)—simultaneous strengthening of one currency and weakening of the other on a single pair.
data_needed: WPR(14) on all pairs of both currency baskets; arithmetic mean then (x+50)*2 remap; distance series; levels ±60.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY H1 worked example (EUR vs JPY baskets); also H4/D1 monitoring CSV for CHF event; overbought 60 / oversold −60.
why_new_for_mis: Senses pair trend change from relative basket-currency strength differential rather than single-pair WPR.
quote: EUR is strengthening and JPY is weakening simultaneously. This event increases the probability of a reversal and moving in a favorable direction.

mechanism: Apply SMA to the dual-currency WPR distance; candle-close crosses of distance vs MA are traded only in Zone#1 (buy) or Zone#2 (sell), ignored in Zone#0 (beyond OB/OS toward borders) and Zone#3 (near zero ±10% flat/equal-strength).
data_needed: Distance buffer + MA(period e.g. 10); zone boundaries at ±60 and ±10.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY with combined EUR/JPY WPR distance; Daily screenshot for MA crosses.
why_new_for_mis: Adds a zoned MA-cross regime sensor on relative currency strength, with explicit flat/equal-power exit band.
quote: Only two zones are suitable for trading when using the pattern #5: Zone #1 for buying ... Zone #2 for selling.

mechanism: Iterate from the newest bar: find alternating peaks/bottoms separated by at least delta_points; first extremum uses fractional threshold first_extrem×delta; then check_min/check_max refine true High/Low in each segment—extrema scale with price variation, not fixed bar count.
data_needed: High/Low arrays over `bars` lookback; delta_points; first_extrem in (0,1); reload_time.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any MT5 symbol; examples with 60/30/120/160 pip variation ranges; intraday vs long-term by choosing delta.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a recent-history-biased, amplitude-gated swing sensor that avoids fractal over-detection in flats and under-detection in volatile bursts.
quote: the variation range is defined as a minimum price change in points between the two neighboring extreme points — the peak and the bottom.

mechanism: R/S analysis on log returns: partition N bars into subgroup sizes, compute mean R/S per size, regress log(R/S) on log(n) for H; compare to E(H) from Anis–Lloyd expectation. H≫0.5±2σ → persistent trend regime; H≪0.5 → anti-persistent mean-reverting; H≈0.5 → random walk.
data_needed: Close series (≥1001 bars for script); log returns; subgroup sizes {10..N}; E(R/S) and Var(H).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Tables for EURUSD, EURCHF, EURJPY, EURGBP, USDJPY, etc. on D1/H4/H1/M15/M5; NZDCHF H1/H2/M30 case study; stocks/commodities also tabulated.
why_new_for_mis: Provides a statistically tested persistence/anti-persistence regime label with significance vs E(H), usable as a market-memory regime feature.
quote: If the Hurst exponent is between 0.5 and 1, and it differs from the expected value by two and more standard deviations, the process is characterized by a long-term memory. In other words, there is persistence.

mechanism: Plot geometric-mean basket indices for both legs of a pair with MAs; enter only when one index crosses its MA in the strengthening direction while the other crosses oppositely (weakening) at candle close within a limited delay—same-direction dual crosses imply flat and are skipped.
data_needed: Basket index series for base and quote (geometric mean of directed closes); MA period (e.g. 10); cross timestamps and max allowed lag.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 with USD and EUR index+MA; joint use with combined WPR distance from Part I.
why_new_for_mis: Extends basket sensing into a dual-index opposite-cross regime-change filter that rejects same-direction (flat) co-moves.
quote: It is recommended to enter the market when one of the currencies becomes weaker, while the second one gets stronger. One of the first signals of that is an index graph crossing MA.
